root_cause.text: The STM32 USBPHYC probe code in `drivers/phy/st/phy-stm32-usbphyc.c` used a device-tree `reg` value as an index into `usbphyc->phys[]` but only rejected values greater than `usbphyc->nphys`, allowing `index == usbphyc->nphys` to pass and cause an off-by-one out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys)` to `if (ret || index >= usbphyc->nphys)`, and the commit message explicitly states that `index` indexes `usbphyc->phys[]` which has `usbphyc->nphys` elements, so equality is one element out of bounds.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the USB PHY probe to reject out-of-range reg values that equal the number of available PHYs.
intent_record.what: The probe-time validation for the child node's "reg" property changed from rejecting only values greater than `usbphyc->nphys` to rejecting values greater than or equal to `usbphyc->nphys`.
intent_record.how: This prevents an out-of-bounds PHY index from being accepted when `index` equals the number of available PHYs, which would otherwise allow an invalid array access or misconfiguration during USB PHY controller probing.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the USB PHY probe to reject out-of-range reg values that equal the number of available PHYs.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes the STM32 USBPHYC probe's bounds check so a device-tree reg value equal to nphys is rejected, preventing the off-by-one out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: This bounds check is off by one: it rejects indices greater than nphys but still accepts index == nphys, which can then be used to index usbphyc->phys[] out of bounds.

vuln_statements.explanation: This bounds check is off by one: it only rejects indices greater than nphys, so index == nphys is accepted and later used to access usbphyc->phys[] out of bounds.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 94c358da3a0545205c6c6a50ae26141f1c73acfa
Author: Amelie Delaunay <amelie.delaunay@st.com>
Date:   Fri Mar 2 15:56:25 2018 +0100

    phy: stm32: add support for STM32 USB PHY Controller (USBPHYC)
    
    This patch adds phy transceiver driver for STM32 USB PHY Controller
    (USBPHYC) that provides dual port High-Speed phy for OTG (single port)
    and EHCI/OHCI host controller (two ports).
    One port of the phy is shared between the two USB controllers through
    a UTMI+ switch.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `stm32_usbphyc_probe()`: `ret = of_property_read_u32(child, "reg", &index); if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys) { ... }`. The root cause is an off-by-one bounds check on the device-tree `reg` value used as an index into `usbphyc->phys[]`. This code only rejects values strictly greater than `nphys`, so `index == usbphyc->nphys` is allowed and later stored in `usbphyc->phys[port]->index = index;`, which is the buggy condition. The fix is not present here because the comparison is still `>` rather than `>=`, so the off-by-one case remains unchecked.
